case_name: Messrs Jetha Bai and Sons, Jew Town, Cochin and Others v Messrs Sunderdas Rathenai and Others
petitioner: Messrs Jetha Bai and Sons, Jew Town, Cochin and Others
facts: The appeals have been clubbed together and listed for consideration of a common question of law involved in them, viz. whether against an order of a District Court in revision u/s. 20 of the Kerala Building (Lease & Rent) Control Act 2 of 1965 (for short the Kerala Act), a further revision would lie to the High Court u/s. 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

The question is not res integra in view of the decision of this Court in Aundal Ammal v. Sadasivan Pillai, [1987] 1 SCC 133: AIR 1987 SC 203 1986 Indlaw SC 605, the appeals have been listed for consideration by a Bench of three Judges of the very same question in order to see whether there is any conflict between the views taken in Aundal Ammal's case 1986 Indlaw SC 605 (supra) and a later decision of this Court in Shyamaraju Hedge v. G. Venkatesha Bhat & Ors., [1987] 3 J.T. 663 1987 Indlaw SC 28419
petitioner_arguments: The relevant passage in the judgment is in the following terms: 'In our opinion, the Full Bench misconstrued the provisions of sub-s. (5) of S. 18 of the Act. Sub-s. (5) of S. 18 clearly states that such decision of the appellate authority as mentioned in S. 18 of the Act shall not be liable to be questioned except in the manner u/s. 20 of the Act.'
respondent_arguments: The Full Bench held that since the District Court exercising revisional powers under S. 20(1) of the Kerala Act functions as a Court and not as a persona designate, the ordinary incidence of the procedure of that Court including any right of appeal or revision will be inhered to the decision rendered by the District Court.
court_reasoning: The Bench drew support for its conclusion from an earlier decision of this Court in Veshesh Kumar v. Shanti Prasad, [1980] 3 SCR 32: 1980(2) SCC 378: AIR 1980 SC 892 1980 Indlaw SC 322.
holding: The Bench held that the ratio laid down by the Kerala High Court in Vareed's case 1968 Indlaw KER 132 (supra) cannot be approved because the High Court had not properly construed Ss. 18(5) and 20 of the Kerala Act.
